{{Quote|This is ''our'' moment. Channel your fury. Destroy our enemies!|Darth Angral, during the [[Sacking of Coruscant]]|<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" />}}
'''Darth Angral''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] serving the resurgent [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] during the time of the [[Great Galactic War]]. Known across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for his lust for blood, he led the [[Sacking of Coruscant]] and killed [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Berooken]] himself. He was one of the Sith Lords that felt offended by the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] that followed afterwards.

During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], Angral sent his son, [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]], to infiltrate the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and steal the [[Planet Prison]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. When Tarnis was killed at the hands of a [[Hero of Tython|rising]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]], Angral vowed to unleash his vengeance across the entire galaxy.

In his quest for revenge, Angral sent his subordinates and [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentices]] to combine more components with the Planet Prison for his latest weapon: the [[Desolator (superweapon)|Desolator]]. With it, he would destroy the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the Republic by taking out a single planet. However, it came at a cost: [[Watcher One]] was apprehended by the Knight who killed Tarnis; his apprentices [[Sadic]] and [[Nefarid]] were killed; and [[Praven]] was turned to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]] and welcomed by the Jedi. Despite the losses, Angral had what he needed.

After [[Devastation of Uphrades|testing]] the firepower of the Desolator on [[Uphrades]], Angral set his sights on the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]. The Knight and their [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Kira Carsen]], boarded Angral's flagship [[Oppressor (Harrower-class)|''Oppressor'']] and confronted the waiting Sith Lord. There, the [[Emperor's Voice|Voice]] of the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] possessed Carsen as she was one of his [[Children of the Emperor|Children]], commanding Angral to destroy the Knight. Angral fought hard in the Emperor's name, but he was no match for the strength of the Jedi who would become known as the Hero of Tython.

==Biography==
===The Great Galactic War===
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], the man who assumed the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] title of Darth Angral had already risen to the rank of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] within the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] by the second decade of the [[Great Galactic War]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3660 BBY]], an Imperial force under the leadership of [[Darth/Legends|Darths]] [[Darth Malgus|Malgus]] and [[Darth Venemal|Venemal]] [[Battle of Ord Radama|attacked]] [[Ord Radama/Legends|Ord Radama]], besieging the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city of [[Livien Magnus]]. However, the [[Dark Council]] decided to send Lord [[Adraas]] to assist in their operations, angering Malgus by exhibiting a lack of trust in his and Venemal's chances. Adraas' attempt to capture the city with [[Battle droid/Legends|war droids]] ended in failure, but Venemal was able to utilize Adraas' assault as a distraction and breach the city walls, resulting in an Imperial victory. Malgus was disgusted when Adraas claimed the credit for the victory when he delivered the news to Darth Angral.<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

Just under seventy days later, the Republic took advantage of the [[Battle on the Hydian Way|breaking]] of the [[Blockade of the Hydian Way|Blockade]] of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] to [[Battle of Korriban (3660 BBY)|strike]] at the Sith holy world of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], though Darth Malgus<ref name="Book of Sith" /> and [[Darth Marr]]<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> were able to repel the short assault. However, the Republic withdrew and attacked their true target of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], initiating the [[Battle of Ziost]] and trapping Darths Angral,<ref name="Book of Sith" /> Marr,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and Malgus on Ziost's surface. The Republic's bombers and interceptors struck at the Sith forces daily, destroying vital arsenals and laser batteries. Believing that the two forces were evenly matched, Angral began to requisition more vessels from the Imperial capital of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]].<ref name="Book of Sith" />

The Dark Councilor Marr proved instrumental in shattering the Republic offensive,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> while the additional ships requested by Darth Angral drove the Republic fleet from Ziost's skies. The next year, the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] himself ordered Darth Malgus to recapture Ord Radama, which Malgus had lost after the [[Death/Legends|death]] of Venemal and the destruction of many of his ships not long after the taking of Livien Magnus. The [[Reconquest of Ord Radama]], as the second battle came to be known, lasted over 50 days, costing Malgus favor with Angral and the Dark Council because of the slow pace of the conflict.<ref name="Book of Sith" />

====The Sacking of Coruscant====
[[File:Angral_vs_Orgus.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Lord Angral engages Orgus Din in combat.]]
Near the end of the war, Darth Angral was selected to personally lead the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] that would attack the Republic capital of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in [[3653 BBY]], taking advantage of [[Alderaan peace conference|sham peace negotiations]] on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] to lure the Republic into a false sense of security. By this time, Angral had developed an intense rivalry with fellow Sith Lord [[Darth Baras]], who had been selected to represent the Empire at the negotiations.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" /> Darth Malgus was chosen to lead a smaller strike force that would be dispatched to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] before Angral's arrival, though Angral insisted that [[Adraas]]&mdash;by then a political ally of his&mdash;serve as Malgus' second-in-command over Malgus' protests.<ref name="Deceived">''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''</ref>

As the [[Planetary shield/Legends|defense grid]] protecting Coruscant was located inside the Jedi Temple and would have to be disabled before Angral's fleet could begin the attack,<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" /> Malgus entered the Temple itself to serve as a distraction while the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae Vizla]] infiltrated the structure to access the grid. Malgus was supported by a strike team of fifty other Sith, who crashed a hijacked [[NR2 gully jumper]] into the front of the Temple and joined their leader in battle. When all of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] defenders of the Temple were dead, the Sith under Malgus and Adraas' leadership destroyed the defense grid's mainframe and Adraas signaled their success to Darth Angral.<ref name="Deceived" /><ref name="Deceived trailer">{{TORweb|url=info/media/trailers/deceived-cinematic-trailer|text=Deceived Cinematic Trailer|int=Deceived}}</ref>

Angral immediately directed his [[Imperial Navy (Sith Empire)|fleet]] to enter the [[Coruscant system/Legends|Coruscant system]], and the Sith began approaching the planet. However, they were contacted by [[Orbital Security Station Six]], a [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security]] [[Space station/Legends|space station]] monitoring incoming traffic to the planet.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" />

[[File:Angral_vs_chancellor_JMGD.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Lord Angral killing Supreme Chancellor Berooken.]]
After destroying Orbital Security Station Six, he landed on the surface near the [[Senate Building/Legends|Galactic Senate Building]], where he was greeted by [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Orgus Din]], who engaged him in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]]. Angral quickly took the upper hand but Din escaped with his life after the [[Sacking of Coruscant|duel]] was interrupted by a crashing Sith [[Starship/Legends|spacecraft]]. Angral then stormed the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]] and attacked [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Berooken]], murdering him live on a [[Holofeed/Legends|holofeed]] to the Republic delegates on Alderaan,<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" /> [[Sai cha/Legends|slicing his head off]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> His attack forced the Republic diplomats on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] to submit to the Sith's demands, and the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] was signed.<ref name="Deceived" />

Angral made his headquarters in the [[Chancellor's working office/Legends|Galactic Senate Chamber Holding Office]]. Darth Malgus was escorted there by Captain [[Roon Neele]]. Within, he quickly began to question the Treaty of Coruscant in an emotional outburst before his superior. Unknown to Malgus, Adraas had beaten him to Angral's command post, and the inferior Lord's presence made the meeting into a major embarrassment for Malgus. The angered Sith was unpracticed in Imperial politics unlike his two contemporaries, who hoped to use Darth Malgus' love for the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]], [[Eleena Daru]], and disapproval of the Emperor's policies as political leverage against him. As their tense conversation progressed, Adraas revealed that he had refused Daru treatment aboard the Steadfast and instead redirected her to one of the civilian hospitals on Coruscant's surface. Upon hearing his rival call Daru a "mongrel," Malgus drew his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and crossed blades with Adraas' own. Angral ended the fight and sent Malgus away to find his lover, but kept Adraas in his offices in a clear showing of where his favor lay.<ref name="Deceived" /> Unknown to Malgus, Angral wanted to see the Jedi destroyed as much as he did and held no favor for the treaty,<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" /><ref name="Race to the Ruins" /> but the superior Sith Lord most likely kept this to himself.

Via holotransmitter, Angral later ordered Malgus aboard the latter's flagship, the [[Valor (Imperial-class)|''Valor'']], to take command of the Imperial blockade and secure the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace lanes]]. Malgus felt that this was insulting after his significant victory in the Jedi Temple, but nonetheless obeyed.<ref name="Deceived" />

As the peace talks were reaching an end, Angral got word that one of the Jedi delegates, [[Aryn Leneer]], had disappeared from Alderaan without reporting any intention whatsoever and was suspected to be heading for Coruscant. The Jedi who had delivered this news to Baras was Master [[Dar'Nala]],<ref name="Deceived" /> who held bitter resentment towards the Sith.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" />

Malgus reported to Angral that a certain [[Zeerid Korr|spicerunner]] was attempting to get past the blockade, censoring only the mention of a Jedi aboard the [[Fatman|freighter]]. The latter Sith Lord mentioned the news of Aryn Leneer and ordered the former to eliminate the young Jedi if she was indeed trying to get to Coruscant, while within his reach. Malgus secretly disobeyed Angral in some small way, but was all too glad to finish off the Jedi, anyway.<ref name="Deceived" />

====Unrest during the Treaty====
{{Quote|&hellip;never again will I stay my hand when the destruction of the Republic and the Jedi is within my reach.''"<br />"''Never again will that be necessary. I assure you.|Lords Angral and Baras|<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" />}}
[[File:CrystalCaveSkirmish-US.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Darth Angral [[Skirmish in the Ancient Crystal Cave|faces]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Harron Tavus]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]].]]
Angral returned to [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] after the treaty's signing. Angral was furious with Darth Baras, who had just finished delivering his report to the [[Dark Council]]. Angral reasoned that if Baras hadn't ended the negotiations so quickly, he could have destroyed all the Jedi on Coruscant. Baras responded by saying he was following [[Tenebrae|their emperor's]] orders, and blasted Angral with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], forcing him into submission. Angral said he wouldn't hesitate the next time he had a chance to destroy the Jedi and Republic, regardless of orders. Baras simply told him such hesitation would never again be necessary.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" />

After his confrontation with Baras, Angral traveled to a business meeting in the [[Star Cluster Casino]] on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] to make an offer. One of the members present was the notorious [[Nok Drayen]], who introduced the Sith Lord.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" />

When a [[Imperial military transport|Sith shuttle]] exploded at the Sith Academy on Korriban, Angral blamed the attack on Republic spies, claiming that the Republic was already reneging on the treaty. These actions aroused Baras' suspicions.<ref name="Threat of Peace 2">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 2: New Galactic Order]]''</ref>
Angral was later traveling to [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]] when he received word that Baras had been behind the attack on the [[Envoy (Republic transport ship)|''Envoy'']]. Angral at first didn't believe this, but then realized that it was the truth when he remembered that the captain of the Imperial ship that had fired on the ''Envoy'' had conveniently been killed in the bombing on Korriban. He then gave the order for his vessel to return to Korriban. Sometime later, he learned that Baras was trying to frame him by telling the Dark Council that he was behind the disruption of the treaty.<ref name="Threat of Peace 3">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 3: Uncertain Surrender]]''</ref>
Upon returning to Korriban, Baras and Angral confronted each other. During a brief duel, Angral revealed that he had discovered that Baras was behind the disruption of the treaty. Baras ended the fight, revealed the truth to Angral (the rogue Jedi Master Dar'Nala was really behind the disruption of the treaty and trying to frame Baras for it) and then tried to persuade Angral over to his side so his plans to corrupt [[Satele Shan]] (whom he correctly believed to be the descendant of [[Revan/Legends|Revan]]) could work.<ref name="Threat of Peace 3" />

Angral accompanied Baras to Dantooine, where they were ambushed by the Jedi Dar'Nala and [[Fortris Gall]], the Republic soldier [[Harron Tavus]], and the [[Mind trick/Legends|controlled]] bounty hunter [[Dalborra]] in the crystal caves. Angral defended himself against Gall, Tavus, and Dalborra while Baras fought Dar'Nala. When Satele Shan joined the fight, Baras put his plan to corrupt her into action: he revealed that Dar'Nala, Satele's master, was behind the disruption of the treaty, including the attack on the ''Envoy''. Baras used this revelation to try to persuade Satele to join the Sith.<ref name="Threat of Peace 3" />

During the battle, Angral tried to kill Tavus by [[Telekinesis/Legends#Saber Throw|throwing]] his lightsaber at him. Tavus managed to evade the attack and wounded the now vulnerable Sith Lord with a grenade. But he refrained from killing him because Satele warned him that would be playing right into the Sith's hands. While Angral was unconscious, Dar'Nala revealed the full extent of her madness when she moved to murder Tavus to punish Satele. This ultimately led to her murder at Dalborra's hands.<ref name="Threat of Peace 3" />

Angral regained consciousness after Dar'Nala's death, and attacked Tavus. Satele came to his defense and declared the fight over. While Angral wanted to continue the battle, Baras (who still wanted Satele in the Sith), allowed them to leave. This irritated Angral, who declared his short-lived alliance with Baras over after their adversaries left.<ref name="Threat of Peace 3" />

===Cold War===
====The Desolator Crisis====
{{Quote|Tell your pathetic Masters that Darth Angral has returned. This time, there will be no mercy.|Darth Angral|<ref name="Race to the Ruins" />}}
[[File:Tarnis_Sadic_Holo.png|thumb|180px|Angral watches his son, [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]], face Orgus Din's [[Hero of Tython|former apprentice]].]]
After the Treaty, the galaxy descended into a [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] that lasted more than a decade. By [[3643 BBY]], Angral had taken on two more students in Lords [[Nefarid]] and [[Sadic]],<ref name="Race to the Ruins" /> and his son [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]] had been trained as a Sith Lord by Angral's apprentice Praven.<ref name="Desert Duel">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Desert Duel|Tatooine}}</ref> Also by that time, Tarnis had infiltrated the Republic under the alias of "Doctor Eli Tarnis", a Republic scientist who was working on the [[Planet Prison]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] project on Coruscant. As the project neared completion, the research team was about to begin field tests when Tarnis hired thieves to steal the design files for the weapon and the other Republic weapons projects.<ref name="Stolen Secrets">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Stolen Secrets|Coruscant}}</ref> Tarnis then staged his own kidnapping by the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] criminal syndicate, trading them advanced Imperial weapons and armor in return for distracting the Republic<ref name="The Rescue">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|The Rescue|Coruscant}}</ref> while Tarnis escaped with the Planet Prison prototype.<ref name="Tracking Down the Traitor">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Tracking Down the Traitor|Coruscant}}</ref> Tarnis fled to the ruins of the Jedi Temple, where he began to set up the device in the [[Jedi Council Chamber/Legends|Jedi Council Chamber]] and contacted his father and Angral's apprentices.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" />

However, a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]&mdash;the latest [[Hero of Tython|former apprentice]] of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Orgus Din]]&mdash;had been pursuing the thieves<ref name="Stolen Secrets" /> and Tarnis' kidnappers, and had learned of Tarnis' true identity as a Sith Lord.<ref name="The Rescue" /> The Knight followed Tarnis to the Temple with the [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Kira Carsen]], and interrupted the traitor's conversation with Angral and the three apprentices. Angral urged Tarnis to ignore the Knight's offer of surrender, and watched as his son unleashed a blast of [[Color/Legends|violet]] [[Force lightning/Legends|lightning]] at the two Jedi. The Sith and his apprentices watched as Tarnis fought fiercely, but was eventually overpowered by the Jedi, and Angral became stricken with fury and grief when the Knight struck down his son. Consumed by rage, Angral choked out a dire warning to the young Jedi, promising to destroy everything and everyone in his path until he gained his revenge. Nefarid gloated that they already controlled the Republic's weapon facilities, and Angral promised to use that power in his war against the Jedi and the Republic.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" />

Angral later flooded Republic comm channels with his vows of vengeance. While the Empire disavowed Angral's actions, General [[Var Suthra]] suspected it to be a lie.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" />

Angral's lust for revenge knew no bounds. One such instance was when his retainer, [[Ferav]], caught the Knight's new Padawan Kira Carsen on the [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] orbital station, she told them that her Master was on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and Angral believed her. Little did he know that her Master was in fact on Ord Mantell, infiltrating an Imperial outpost for information on his plans.<ref name="Missing Intelligence">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Missing Intelligence|Ord Mantell}}</ref>

[[Watcher One]] of [[Imperial Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Imperial Intelligence]] encountered the Knight on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] in a race to find Doctor [[Nasan Godera]], one of the brains behind the Republic superweapons. Though Watcher One was able to get Gedora's information and transmitted it to Angral, the Dark Lord was not pleased to learn that Watcher One had made a compromise with his son's killer. He ordered the agent to subdue the Knight to be shipped to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] with Gedora so he could execute the former himself, but Watcher One failed.<ref name="Catching up with Watcher One">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Catching up with Watcher One|Taris}}</ref>

Later, Angral ordered Lord Praven to use the [[Shock Drum]] superweapon to destroy [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to kill his adversary, even destroy its deactivation code so the Knight's mission would end in failure if the Jedi managed to reach the superweapon. However, Praven, being the honorable Sith he was, disobeyed his master and made a new code reserved for a [[Duel on the Esus Mesa|duel]] with the Knight. When he was defeated, he surrendered the destruction code and went to turn himself in to the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], in which he was redeemed.<ref name="Desert Duel" />

====Uphrades and Showdown====
{{Quote|Angral's dead&mdash;and this battle cruiser's not far behind him.''"<br />"''Disappointing. Angral was useful.|The [[Hero of Tython|Jedi Knight]] and [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] speak of Angral after his death.|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" />}}
[[File:Orgus_captured.png|thumb|left|200px|Darth Angral prepares to kill his old enemy, Orgus Din.]]
Eventually, Angral took the plans of the Planet Prison and other superweapons which he used to create the [[Desolator (superweapon)|Desolator]]. Master Orgus Din, who had earlier misled the [[Hero of Tython]] into believing he was after another objective, so his former Padawan wouldn't have a chance to join him, boarded the [[Oppressor (Harrower-class)|''Oppressor'']] and tried to stop the Sith Lord, but Angral was too strong and overpowered his enemy. He expressed disappointment that Orgus didn't bring his pupil, boasting that he could destroy them both. Orgus urged Angral to do the right thing for once and surrender, which the Dark Lord arrogantly refused. As he drew his lightsaber, Angral asked Orgus if he was afraid to die, to which he replied, "There is no death. There is only the Force." Angral then impaled his old nemesis, demanding to know if that belief was true, where was his son. In way of a taunt, Nefarid revealed the confrontation and Din's death recorded as a holomessage to the Hero of Tython. Angral broadcast Orgus' execution over the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] and left the body floating in space at the edge of the [[Alderaan system/Legends|Alderaan system]] for the Republic to find.<ref name="Facing Lord Nefarid" />

Angral tested his new weapon on the Republic's farm world of [[Uphrades]], resulting in the planet's total destruction. Some civilians, on the other hand, managed to survive.<ref name="Uphrades">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Uphrades|Uphrades}}</ref> Nevertheless, Angral used the [[Speciecide|genocide]] to draw the Knight to him.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" />

[[File:AngryAngral-TOR.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Darth Angral, moments before his death.]]
Angral then attempted to use the Desolator on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], aiming to finish the Jedi Order. The Knight, as well as the Padawan Kira Carsen, infiltrated the weapon and disabled it. As the Jedi confronted him on the bridge of the ''Oppressor'', Angral refused to let his triumph be stolen, even though it was apparent that he was beaten. As the Dark Lord and his foe prepared to fight, the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] possessed Kira and ordered Angral to finish the job. Angral agreed to his supreme Master's wishes. As the Emperor's control over Kira faded, Angral urged her to join him, claiming it to be her destiny to be Sith. Kira refused. Angral then dueled against both Jedi Knight and Padawan but was no match for the two combined.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" />

As the wounded Angral reached for his blade, the Emperor decided to take matters into his hands. He retook control of Kira and engaged the Knight, during which Angral died from his wounds. When the Knight announced this, the Emperor was disappointed.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Behold the teachings of Darth Angral, Lord of the Sith!|Darth Angral in his holocron|<ref name="Apprentice">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Inquisitor|The Apprentice|Taris}}</ref>}}
At some time before his death, Angral created a [[Darth Angral's holocron|holocron]], which was found on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] by [[Darth Nox]].<ref name="Apprentice" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Darth Angral was the spark that lit the flame. Even in failure, he inspired the Sith to violence.|[[Bela Kiwiiks]] speaks of Angral's influence on the Sith.|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" />}}
[[File:Angral-TORTOPV1.jpg|thumb|left|222px|Darth Angral]]
Darth Angral had been a complete loose cannon in the Sith Empire. He wanted to see the Jedi and Republic be destroyed, but he knew that he had to obey the Dark Council, even if it meant keeping peace with the enemy, which disgusted him.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" /> However, the peace offered by the Treaty of Coruscant caused a change in Angral, who went from a bloodthirsty warlord to a master schemer. His bold and cunning plans were noted to be on par with those of Imperial Intelligence.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> Like many Sith Lords, Angral viewed [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] as nothing more than second-class citizens and slaves in the Empire. He made sure to let Darth Malgus know that. Angral was not one to lead without controlling his minions. While making his headquarters in the late Supreme Chancellor's office on Coruscant, he ordered Adraas and Darth Malgus to stop their duel.<ref name="Deceived" /> Angral showed himself to be a supporting father to his son, Tarnis. When he watched him die via hologram, he vowed to make Tarnis' killer pay by killing countless innocent civilians and hold the Hero of Tython responsible for it.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" /> When the Knight confronted him about Uphrades, Angral freely admitted that he had done so to challenge the knight to a confrontation. Despite his lust for independent slaughter, Angral remained true to the Sith Emperor until his death.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" />

==Powers and abilities==
[[File:Angral_lightsaber.png|thumb|150px|Angral's lightsaber]]
Darth Angral was skilled in lightsaber combat, as well as his knowledge of the Force, being able to quickly defeat Jedi Master Orgus Din, although prevented from finishing him off by an explosion which allowed Din to escape. Angral later attacked Darth Baras, after the latter had consulted the Dark Council, only to be quickly overpowered.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" /> He was also skilled in the art of [[Telekinesis/Legends#Saber throw|saber throw]].<ref name="Threat of Peace 3" /> Angral was adept at launching Force lightning at his opponents. He could combine this ability with [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Whirlwind|Force whirlwind]]. He could even produce a lightning shield.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" /> When Angral met up with Orgus Din again aboard the ''Oppressor'', he defeated him once more, this time killing him.<ref name="Facing Lord Nefarid" /> Despite all his skill, Angral was no match for the Hero of Tython and Kira Carsen. However, he was considered by the Emperor himself to be one of his more useful servants.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" />
